snip.t: There is an increased risk for phimosis and for balanitis in uncircumcised males.
Penile lesions: balanitis, phimosis, warts (HPV), herpes, syphilitic chancre, squamous cell carcinoma (see the penile notes), and penile curvature (chordee, Peyronie's).
snip.s: Urology: History, Examination and Common Presenting Symptoms

snip.t: Penis: foreskin (phimosis, paraphimosis, balanitis, balanitis xerotica obliterans/lichen sclerosus), the external meatus (hypospadias, meatal stenosis, discharge), the shaft (plaques of Peyronie's, lesions), and the glans (cancer).
snip.s: Urology: History, Examination and Common Presenting Symptoms

snip.t: Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus (balanitis xerotica obliterans, BXO): a chronic, progressive sclerosing dermatosis of the glans and prepuce, usually in uncircumcised men: white atrophic patches, phimosis, itching, painful erections, and meatal and urethral strictures.
snip.s: Penile Conditions: Benign Lesions, Premalignant Disease and Penile Cancer

snip.t: | Anterior urethra | Strictures, meatal stenosis, phimosis, hypospadias, urethral stones, tumours, penile trauma, foreign body |
snip.s: Urethral Stricture and Acute Urinary Retention

snip.t: Balanitis/Balanoposthitis — poor hygiene, smegma irritant; Phimosis — prepuce can't retract
snip.s: Exam Prep: Skin Infections, Psoriasis & Pemphigus

snip.t: Phimosis — prepuce cannot be retracted over glans; congenital OR acquired (from balanoposthitis scarring).
snip.s: Quick Guide: Male Reproductive System Pathology, Testis, Penis — Notes

qs.q: A 58‑year‑old uncircumcised man presents with painful erections, white atrophic patches on the glans, phimosis and a meatal stricture. What is the most appropriate initial therapy?
qs.e: Topical clobetasol can improve early disease but does not reverse established scarring. Buccal graft addresses the stricture, not the inflammatory skin changes.
